claim.why_it_matters: Plain paragraph rather than a heading, while its siblings 4.2.2.1.1 and 4.2.2.1.4 are '####' headings; the outline loses the Reserved Words clause IV.4.2.2.1.3.

verdict.reasoning: The rendered PDF page 154 (folio IV-8) prints '4.2.2.1.3 Reserved Words' as a stand-alone clause heading, set flush left with the title in bold, in the same style as 4.2.2.1.2 System-Names and 4.2.2.1.3.1 Required Words. In specs/ANSI_COBOL_1985.md, line 6525 holds it as plain paragraph text. Its siblings are marked as headings: line 6429 is '#### 4.2.2.1.1 User-Defined Words' and line 6587 is '#### 4.2.2.1.4 Function-Names'. The words match exactly, so no text is lost. The heading markup is missing, though, so the clause IV.4.2.2.1.3 drops out of the markdown outline. That is a genuine structural discrepancy and not just line wrapping or page furniture. The claim also understates the scope: on the same page, '4.2.2.1.2 System-Names' (line 6513) and '4.2.2.1.3.1 Required Words' are plain paragraphs too, even though the PDF prints them as headings.
verdict.corrected_description: The markdown holds '4.2.2.1.3 Reserved Words' (line 6525) as a plain paragraph, but the PDF prints it as a clause heading, and its siblings 4.2.2.1.1 and 4.2.2.1.4 are '####' headings. The text is identical, so only the outline structure is affected. On the same page, 4.2.2.1.2 System-Names and 4.2.2.1.3.1 Required Words also lack heading markup.
